Update a tag

How to Update an Ollama Model with ollama pull

Run ollama list to find the full library tag, then run ollama pull NAME:TAG again. If you need to keep the current version, first copy it to a new local tag with ollama cp. Compare the model ID before and after, then run a prompt you already know works.

  1. Identify the installed model
  2. Update a library tag
  3. Rebuild a custom tag
  4. Check the update
  5. Restore the previous version
  6. See the rollback test

Where did the model tag come from?

Pull againRebuildCheck tag

Identify the tag and the server

Use the exact name from ollama list, including the part after the colon. Check that the CLI is reaching the same Ollama server as your app. For a Docker install, run commands in the server container or point your CLI at its API address.

Check the Ollama model library for the tag you originally pulled. If you used ollama create, imported a GGUF or made a copy with ollama cp, check your local recipe or the original library name first. A custom tag can have the same name as a library tag.

ollama --version checks the Ollama software version. A model pull refreshes a model tag. If a model requires a newer Ollama release, follow the Ollama setup instructions before retrying.

Update a library model with ollama pull

Record the installed tag and ID. Replace qwen2.5:0.5b with your model if it differs. Choose a backup tag you have never used and confirm it has the original ID before you pull the library tag again.

ollama list
ollama cp qwen2.5:0.5b qwen2.5:before-update-20261128
ollama list

Once requests using the model have finished, unload its running copy and pull the same exact library tag.

ollama stop qwen2.5:0.5b
ollama pull qwen2.5:0.5b
ollama list

The server needs access to the registry and room for any new files. If the pull fails, keep the backup and check the error, server and free space before retrying. Changing to a different tag selects a different library entry. In particular, :latest can differ from the tag you currently use.

Refresh a custom model or imported GGUF

Keep the old local tag with ollama cp and keep the original source files. Update the base tag or GGUF path in your Modelfile, then build under a separate candidate tag first. Run your usual prompts against the candidate before changing your app’s model selection.

ollama create my-model:candidate -f Modelfile
ollama run my-model:candidate

See the Modelfile examples for how to check which base and parameters the build uses. Pulling a library base does not rebuild an existing custom tag.

Tell whether the installed model changed

  • Same ID: the prefix shown by ollama list matches. Compare the full digest in GET /api/tags on the same server if you need an exact check.
  • Different digest: the installed model manifest changed. Parameters and templates can change a digest even when the weights are identical.
  • Working update: run a previously listed model with the exact tag. Repeat a known prompt and any app-specific test, such as parsing the JSON or invoking a tool you rely on. A successful pull alone only confirms the transfer and install.

Keep the saved tag until the new version works where you use it. A local copy uses the same model store. To protect against a disk failure, keep a separate copy of the complete models folder.

Roll back to the old Ollama model

The quickest rollback is to point your app to the saved local tag and test it. If the app needs the original tag, wait for active requests to finish. The second command below replaces the model under that original name, so check the source and destination first.

ollama stop qwen2.5:0.5b
ollama cp qwen2.5:before-update-20261128 qwen2.5:0.5b
ollama list

Confirm the original tag’s digest matches the saved tag, then run your known prompt again. If you never saved the earlier version, check for a separate store backup or the exact old source files. Pulling the same library tag again gets the registry’s current version.

What the saved tag retained in an offline test

On macOS arm64 with Ollama 0.40.18, we imported Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M under a temporary tag. We kept a copy, rebuilt the active tag with the same GGUF and a different num_ctx, restarted Ollama, then restored the active tag from the saved copy.

StageActive IDActive num_ctx
Before rebuild29edfba2ee461024
After restart237e3de8d9c92048
After rollback29edfba2ee461024

The saved tag kept ID 29edfba2ee46 and still replied LOCAL_OK after restart. Restoring the active tag brought back the full digest, the original parameter value and the reply. Creating the alias left the sum of blob file lengths unchanged. This was a local rebuild and rollback test using ollama create and ollama cp.

What happened when we pulled a real library tag again?

We used the public smollm:135m tag in a separate store. A local build under that same name had ID 3533754c2af6. After saving the local build, ollama pull smollm:135m installed the registry ID b0b2a4617438. A second pull kept that ID. Copying the saved local build over the active name restored 3533754c2af6.

The registry files were already in the test store after separate checksum-verified downloads. This checks how a real pull changes the local tag and how to reverse it. The local variation stood in for the previous version.
